#!/bin/bash
# Script to ping all hosts in 192.168.1.0/24 range

echo "Starting ping scan of 192.168.1.0/24 network..."

for i in {1..254}; do
    ip="192.168.1.$i"
    echo -n "$ip: "
    if ping -c 1 -W 1 "$ip" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Online"
    else
        echo "Offline"
    fi
done

echo "Ping scan completed."

arguments.newText:
#!/bin/bash

# Script to ping all IP addresses in 192.168.1.0/24 range
# and check common ports on active hosts

# Output file for results
OUTPUT_FILE="network_scan_results.txt"

# Clear previous results
> "$OUTPUT_FILE"

# Function to check if a port is open using bash built-in
check_port() {
    local host=$1
    local port=$2
    local timeout=1
    
    # Use bash built-in /dev/tcp to check connectivity
    if (echo > /dev/tcp/$host/$port) >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Port $port open"
    else
        echo "Port $port closed"
    fi
}

# Add timestamp to results
echo "Network scan started at $(date)" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"
echo "Scanning 192.168.1.0/24 network..." >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"
echo "----------------------------------------" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"

for i in {1..254}
do
    ip="192.168.1.$i"
    echo "Pinging $ip..."
    
    if ping -c 1 -W 1 "$ip" > /dev/null 2>&1
    then
        echo "$ip is active"
        # Log active host
        echo "" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"
        echo "Host: $ip" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"
        echo "Status: ACTIVE" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"
        
        # Check common ports
        echo "Checking ports on $ip..." >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"
        echo "Port 22 (SSH): $(check_port $ip 22)" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"
        echo "Port 80 (HTTP): $(check_port $ip 80)" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"
        echo "Port 443 (HTTPS): $(check_port $ip 443)" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"
    else
        echo "$ip is unreachable"
        # Log unreachable host
        echo "$ip: UNREACHABLE" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"
    fi
done

echo "" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"
echo "Network scan completed at $(date)" >> "$OUTPUT_FILE"
echo "Results saved to $OUTPUT_FILE"
